source.title: Social support and oxytocin interact to suppress cortisol and subjective responses to psychosocial stress

confidence_rationale: Human placebo-controlled experiment (intranasal oxytocin x social support, 2x2, Trier Social Stress Test): social support suppressed salivary free cortisol, oxytocin produced an anxiolytic effect, and the combination produced the lowest cortisol with the highest calmness/lowest anxiety. Provides a causal human mechanistic anchor for SOOTHING as down-regulation of the ONGOING neuroendocrine stress response, mediated by oxytocin and gated by a conspecific -- distinct from relief and safety. claim_ids_tested intentionally empty (no registered soothing mechanism). Source quality good (controlled human pharmacology + validated stressor); mapping fidelity moderate-low (REE lacks an other-model and an HPA/cortisol axis per se); transfer risk moderate-high.
failure_signatures: The soothing effect is strongest at oxytocin x social-support interaction -- it is socially gated, confirming the V4-social scope and the inadequacy of a V3 emotion-by-name build.

The measured output is HPA/cortisol + subjective anxiety down-regulation of an ACTIVE stressor, not an offset reinforcement (relief) or a learned threat-absence prediction (safety) -- mis-assigning it to MECH-302/303/304 would corrupt those records.
REE has no cortisol/HPA axis; the proxy is the suffering accumulator (MECH-219) gain/decay and drive (SD-012), so the mapping is by analogy, not by direct substrate correspondence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In healthy men exposed to the Trier Social Stress Test, social support suppressed salivary free cortisol responses, intranasal oxytocin produced an anxiolytic effect, and oxytocin combined with social support yielded the lowest cortisol concentrations together with increased calmness and decreased anxiety; oxytocin appears to enhance the buffering effect of social support on stress reactivity.
mapping.ree_translation: Proposed SOOTHING/COMFORT stream (NOT registered): an oxytocin-mediated, socially-gated down-regulation of the ongoing stress/arousal state. In REE this maps to a state-gain/recovery modulator on the suffering accumulator (MECH-219 decay rate) and homeostatic drive (SD-012; SD-032e autonomic coupling) -- reducing the amplitude/persistence of the active aversive trajectory, distinct from relief (MECH-302 offset reinforcement) and safety (MECH-303/304 prospective prediction).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Human cortisol/HPA + self-report outcomes; REE has neither an HPA axis nor an other-model, so the mapping is analogical (to MECH-219/SD-012 dynamics) and the social trigger is V4-bound. claim_ids_tested empty because no soothing claim exists. The entry grounds the differentiation and the proposed register row, not an REE implementation as written.
mapping.source_context: Human, healthy adult males (n=37), 2x2 intranasal oxytocin (24 IU) x social support, Trier Social Stress Test; salivary cortisol + subjective anxiety/calmness outcomes.

confidence_components.notes: Strong causal human anchor for oxytocin-gated stress down-regulation; held down on REE-mapping fidelity (no HPA axis / other-model in REE). Net 0.76 for 'soothing is a distinct, oxytocin-mediated, socially-gated state-regulation system'.
